problem:
Consider the equation in the variable $z,$ given by

$$
3qz+4=7z+1
$$

where $q$ is a constant. Given that this equation has no solution, what is the value of $q?$

$q=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
Suppose we have an equation of the form

$$
ax=b
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants, and $b\ne 0.$ If $a=0,$ then the equation has no solution.

First, we rewrite the equation in the form $az=b.$ 

We start by subtracting $7z$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}3qz+4 & =7z+1 \\ 3qz-7z+4 & =7z+1-7z \\ 3qz-7z+4 & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we subtract $4$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}3qz-7z+4 & =1 \\ 3qz-7z+4-4 & =1-4 \\ 3qz-7z & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we factor $z$ on the left-hand side. This gives

$$
(3q-7)z=-3.
$$

Notice that this equation is now in the form $az=b:$

$$
{{(3q-7)}_{⏟}}_{a}z={{-3}_{⏟}}_{b}
$$

Therefore, the equation has no solution if

$$
3q-7=0.
$$

Solving this for $q,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3q-7 & =0 \\ 3q-7+7 & =0+7 \\ 3q & =7 \\ \frac{3q}{3} & =\frac{7}{3} \\ q & =\frac{7}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
